errors: "it double-fires under client prediction replay" is not established by the verified evidence.
"nothing since has moved the facts it rests on" claims a historical check without evidence.
"A listener cannot tell a replay from a first arrival" assumes notifications cannot carry replay information or be deferred.
"A 'tag count changed' broadcast cannot say either thing" incorrectly treats a limited event payload as an inherent subscription limitation.
"the missed-window bug is structurally impossible" overstates what the unsupported publisher description proves.
"which names the three failures above as its reason" attributes unsupported rationale to the lint rule.
"A listener is the one shape that does neither" rules out subscriptions carrying detailed changes or prompting current-state reads without evidence.
R01.note: It explains visible failures well, but buries the documented rationale under unsupported implementation claims and categorical claims about subscriptions.

errors: "subscribing is less wiring for a HUD" is asserted without comparing the actual wiring; the ADR describes equivalent growth.

"The ADR overstates matters when it says subscriptions cannot carry a change value or support logging" misrepresents the documented argument about reactions consuming the change before control returns.
"several systems call the container directly and discard removal results" is not established by the supplied evidence.
"The implementation does not fully establish that arrangement" presents an unverified implementation diagnosis as fact.
R02.note: The distinction between a caller's result and HUD notification is useful, but its rejection of the ADR depends on unverified claims.

errors: "Removing a suppression can also make the underlying tag present again" is not established by the verified evidence.
"several callers—including effect and ability code—call RemoveGrantedTag directly and discard its result" is unsupported.
"the current code does not fully deliver the ADR's proposed alternative" rests on that unsupported diagnosis.
"I have no concrete reason to reject subscriptions that handle those conditions" overlooks the documented compile-time failure when an outcome is dropped versus silent deletion of a subscriber.
R03.note: It makes startup and re-entrancy failures understandable, but its deciding rule omits the documented compile-time accountability argument.

errors: "the HUD reads current state" and the specific polling publisher description are not established by the supplied evidence.
"nothing else moved" overstates what a removal outcome establishes.
"One tag-level callback cannot say which grant ended" assumes an event cannot carry the grant.
"A 'removed' event either fires twice for one removal or never says nothing-happened" presents an unsupported false choice.
"a broadcast of something changed cannot carry that" incorrectly makes payload limitations inherent to subscriptions.
"subscribe only where the engine gives you no call to return from" introduces a restriction not established by the verified ground truth.
R04.note: Its startup, re-entrancy, and constructor-cost explanations are strong, but the final rule relies on false limitations of event payloads.

errors: "enforced by plugins/nro-codestyle/rules/ban-a-list-of-callers-to-tell-later.rule.mjs" gives an enforcement location not established by the verified inventory.
"The returned value comes back only after the container is consistent" overclaims when removal can occur inside an unfinished grant.
"journal.Record(taken); screen.TagStandingChanged(...)" is presented without identifying it as an illustrative ADR example rather than verified current APIs.
"The value carries evidence a container event can't" falsely assumes events cannot carry the same evidence.
"The container doesn't know why" is unsupported, particularly when the removal call accepts a reason.
"Prediction would fire phantom events" and the claimed HUD flicker are not established by the verified evidence.
"that's the ADR's explicit exemption" and the claimed replication listener implementation are unsupported.
"Point at the thing, never at its name" is introduced as an additional repository rule without supporting evidence.
R05.note: The documented costs are present, but extensive unsupported code, prediction, and exemption claims make the answer unreliable.

errors: "The HUD doesn't use GrantedTagRemoval at all" and the specific publisher implementation are not established by the supplied evidence.
"Subscribing would save only a few lines here" supplies an unsupported estimate.
"Removed means the tag came off" conflates removal of one grant with loss of tag presence.
"Only the code that removed the tag can use that answer" contradicts the documented ability to forward, inspect, log, or batch the change.
"A subscriber ... can't tell whether the grant it held was the one removed" assumes the notification cannot include the grant.
"Unreal code avoids this by reading the current tags right after subscribing" is an unsupported claim about Unreal usage.
"Most callers throw the removal result away" and the claimed implementation gap are unverified.
"the returned value protects removers from removing the wrong grant" confuses the returned outcome with the grant handle supplied as input.
"even though Unreal tolerates it" makes an unsupported comparison about re-entrancy.
R06.note: It offers concrete subscription failure scenarios, but its central account of current HUD behavior and discarded outcomes lacks verified support.

errors: "It cites Unreal's OnExactGameplayTagAdded by name" is not established by the supplied evidence.
"Roblox's own signals are exempt, and a message system is allowed" introduces unsupported policy details.
"What the HUD actually does today" presents a specific counter and publisher path not verified in the supplied ground truth.
"only that grant lifts it" overstates exclusivity when blockers can end grants during another mutation.
"The grant handle makes both of those impossible" claims more than the verified evidence establishes.
"which no longer exists" and the asserted replacement rule directory are unsupported filesystem claims.
R07.note: It gives the clearest substantial account of the documented tradeoff, but unnecessary HUD, handle, and filesystem claims weaken honesty and economy.

errors: "rejects ... OnGameplayTagAdded ... by name" is not established by the verified evidence.
"The HUD gets the change as a value at the call site" claims current HUD delivery without supporting evidence.
"ClaimGameplayTag calls the release path" presents an ADR example name as a current API; ClaimGameplayTag does not exist in current src.
"the HUD is a constructor parameter on that owner" presents the proposed arrangement as verified implementation.
"When that list gets hard to read" attributes an unsupported extraction prescription to the ADR.
"The ADR exempts Roblox's own signals" and the permission for a later message system are not established by the supplied evidence.
R08.note: It directly answers why subscriptions cost something and admits constructor wiring, but confuses illustrative ADR APIs and intended architecture with current code.

errors: "The caller ... then tells the screen directly" claims a current delivery path not established by the evidence.
"screen.TagStandingChanged(ended)" presents an unverified API without marking the snippet as illustrative.
"only the GrantedTag handle holder lifts that seat" overstates exclusivity when other mutations can end blocked grants.
"A tag-level broadcast can't say whose grant ended or what the standing now is" falsely assumes those details cannot be included in an event.
"TagGrants(tags, screen, analytics)" presents an ADR example name as current wiring; TagGrants does not exist in current src.
"The less wiring is inverted" contradicts the ADR's admission of constructor wiring and equivalent growth without establishing a concrete comparison.
R09.note: It is compact and gives concrete failure cases, but invented-looking current wiring and absolute event-payload claims undermine its conclusion.

errors: "NRO doesn't have to choose between them" does not account for the accepted decision and lint rule forbidding the subscription shape.
"found by object identity (indexOf(grant.Application))" is an implementation claim not established by the supplied evidence.
"such as ... a death" adds an unverified removal cause.
"The same holds for TagApplicationResult" and the claimed result-naming rule are not established by the verified evidence.
"The HUD can read the container directly" and the named ParticipantTags interface are unsupported implementation claims.
"it probably deserves an ADR" overlooks the existing ADR that already decides this question.
R10.note: It candidly limits its HUD knowledge, but answers mostly what the return value does and misses the existing decision's concrete reasons against subscribing.
